draft.title: Relative and absolute dating
card: puts fossils or rock layers in order of age without giving a number of years. It says one is older or younger than another.
In undisturbed layers, lower layers are older than upper layers. A matching index fossil also shows that layers in different places are of similar age.
gives an age in years. It uses radioactive decay, where an unstable isotope changes into another isotope at a steady rate.
The time taken for half of an isotope to decay is its half-life. Measuring how much of it remains in a sample shows how old the sample is.
draft.remember: Relative dating gives an order. Absolute dating gives an age in years from decay.

a.q: A scientist states that fossil X is older than fossil Y because X lies in a lower, undisturbed layer. What type of dating is this?
a.why: The scientist gave an order of age from the position of the layers, with no age in years. That is relative dating. Absolute dating would need a measurement of radioactive decay to give an age in years.
a.clue: Is an age in years given?

b.q: A volcanic rock beside a fossil in Victoria has one quarter of its original isotope left. The half-life is 10 million years. What is the age of the rock?
b.why: One half-life leaves half of the isotope and two half-lives leave one quarter. Two half-lives of 10 million years is 20 million years. 10 million years is tempting but would leave half remaining.
b.clue: Count how many times the amount has halved.

check.summary: No problems found. Both questions have one clearly correct answer that matches the card, and the explanations are accurate.
